alternate_mechanisms.name: patronage_status_exposed_by_account
alternate_mechanisms.summary: Withdrawal from divine allegiance can imply reliance on another patronage or status structure, but compelled return brings every such claim before an account that measures standing rather than accepting inherited or affiliated security.

alternate_mechanisms.name: refusal_as_disavowal_and_non_submission
alternate_mechanisms.summary: The two coordinated verbs describe one refusal in complementary dimensions: withdrawal breaks allegiance, disbelief repudiates truth, and both enact non-submission to the named worshipped sovereign.

alternate_mechanisms.name: distance_cannot_become_escape
alternate_mechanisms.summary: Withdrawal creates relational distance and imagined remoteness, yet return is explicitly oriented to God; final approach reverses direction and prevents moral distance from becoming an independent destination.

alternate_mechanisms.name: typed_refuser_becomes_accountable_class
alternate_mechanisms.summary: The singular relative refuser is first presented as a moral type; the shift to their plural return and account turns that type into a class whose grave liability is collectively subject to adjudication.

alternate_mechanisms.name: uncovered_liability_under_measured_sanction
alternate_mechanisms.summary: The one who covers truth and refuses merciful benefaction does not thereby cover away guilt: the grave liability remains for adjudication, and the greater punishment is enclosed within reckoning rather than presented as unmeasured force.

alternate_mechanisms.name: rejected_support_answered_by_divine_sufficiency
alternate_mechanisms.summary: Human rejection of allegiance and support changes the rejecter's relation to God, not God's capacity or right to undertake the account; عَلَيْنَا frames final judgment as divinely assumed, sufficient responsibility.
